result:
result: "opencode browse" is `@opencode/browse` (repo `anomalyco/browse`), an MCP server (stdio) plus a Chromium extension. Pi can call it through its native MCP support, but it needs a paired, extension-equipped Chromium.

**opencode-browse (sourced, fetched 2026-11-09)**
- Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/browse (README on `dev`), https://opencode.ai/product/browse and https://www.npmjs.com/package/@opencode/browse.
- License is MIT. Latest npm version is 0.0.15, published about 19 hours before fetch. The repo was created 2026-10-27, so it is young and fast-moving, and no pin is stable yet.
- Architecture: the agent talks to `browse mcp` over stdio. That calls a local relay on `127.0.0.1:19988`, which presents a CDP endpoint. The extension drives the user's real browser through `chrome.debugger`.
- `execute` runs Playwright code, using Patchright with a restricted realm. It is not a security boundary.
- Tools: `execute` (with `page`, `snapshot()`, `handoff()`), `session_new/list/use/reset/delete/adopt/allowlist`, `network` (HAR), `recording`, `flight_recorder`, `secrets_*`, `tabs_cleanup`, `settings`, `status`. There are no separate click or type tools.
- Install: `npx @opencode/browse install`, `npm i -g @opencode/browse && browse install`, or `curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/browse/install | bash` (a binary from `anoma.ly`). Node 22.19+ is needed for npx. The installer auto-updates and `browse install` rewrites agent configs.
- Its README lists Pi as a supported agent: `~/.pi/agent/mcp.json`, `{"mcpServers":{"browse":{"command":"browse","args":["mcp"]}}}`. The generic stdio entry is the same.
- Pi MCP: https://pi.dev/docs/latest/mcp says Pi has a native MCP client (stdio and streamable HTTP, `pi mcp add`). Tools are named `mcp__<server>__<tool>`. `pi.registerMcpServer()` registers servers from an extension (per `pi-mcp-extension` docs on pi.dev).
- I found no Pi package wrapping `@opencode/browse`. Third-party `opencode-browser` plugins exist, but they are different projects.
- It can run outside opencode. The README says it works with any MCP client and has a CLI (`browse --help`).
- Limits: it needs a Chromium with the extension installed and paired, so it is not a headless library. Pairing runs through the Chrome Web Store, or a load-unpacked dev build (`npx @opencode/browse@dev install`, then `browse pair`). A relay on another machine is possible through `browse set hostname`.
- Linux headless support is not documented. The README names no Linux or cloud caveat.

**/opt/pw-browsers/chromium (inference)**
- It is probably unusable as-is. It is a Playwright build with no extension and no paired state, and no source says browse can launch or drive an arbitrary Chromium.
- It would work only if the extension is loaded unpacked into it (needs a display or new-headless) and paired. That is untested, and I did not run anything.

**fit (sourced facts, then inference)**
- `pi-computer-use` 0.1.36 (https://pi.dev/packages/@amaster.ai/pi-computer-use) wraps Cua Driver 0.37.0 for macOS, Linux and Windows. It has 62 tools: native input, an accessibility tree, screenshots, recording, and "browser tools". That last group overlaps with browse.
- The T3 tools are `mcp__t3-code__*` preview and HTML render tools. They are injected by T3 and expose no DOM driving (per report assignment-0mw8tdgpq-hfsl, which did not list the T3 tools).
- Recommended split (inference):
  - `pi-computer-use` serves desktop apps and anything outside a browser.
  - browse serves web pages in a real browser, where the user's logins, a human handoff, HAR or recording, or Playwright matter.
  - The T3 tools serve the page the user sees in T3: render and preview only, not automation.
- Overlaps: browsers can be driven by `pi-computer-use`'s browser group and by browse. Prefer browse for page content, because the extension gives a stable session model, handoff and allowlists. Use `pi-computer-use` only for native browser chrome such as dialogs.
- Surfacing browse's lower-level tools or docs wholesale would collide with `computer_use_*` and `mcp__browse__*`, so a single screen capability would have to route between them.
- Under T3 Supervised mode, every extension tool triggers an `Allow X?` confirm.

Not read: the `SKILL.md` in the browse repo, the Linux cloud behavior, the Chrome Web Store listing's Linux support, and the `pi-computer-use` browser group's tool names.
